1	# frai-gate
2	
3	The **FRAI Gate** (Responsible AI Gate) for specs - part of [FRAI](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai).
4	
5	Every spec for an AI-touching feature must contain a complete `## FRAI Gate`
6	section - seven checks - and implementation doesn't start until the gate passes:
7	
8	1. Risk tier (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk requires a named human sign-off)
9	2. Data provenance & privacy
10	3. Human oversight
11	4. Evaluation plan (numeric thresholds)
12	5. Bias & fairness
13	6. Monitoring & rollback
14	7. Transparency & incident response
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```bash
19	npx frai-gate init --ci                 # scaffold FRAI-SPEC.md + a GitHub Action that runs
20	                                        # the gate on every PR (works in any repo)
21	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md         # deterministic validation - no API key needed
22	npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # + adversarial AI review of answer quality
23	npx frai-gate draft                     # read-only agent scans the repo and drafts a
24	                                        # gate section grounded in your actual code
25	```
26	
27	Also available as `frai gate ...` from the main [frai CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai).
28	
29	Exit codes: `0` PASS/WARN · `1` BLOCK · `2` usage/error - drop `frai-gate check` straight into CI.
30	
31	`draft` and `--smart` run on the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk)
32	with read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) and need Claude Code authentication or
33	`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Override the model with `FRAI_GATE_MODEL` (default `claude-opus-5`).
34	
35	> **Privacy note:** `draft` and `--smart` send the repository content the agent reads to
36	> Anthropic's API. The agent is instructed never to read secret material (`.env`, keys,
37	> certificates, credential stores), but treat that as a mitigation, not a guarantee -
38	> think before running them on highly sensitive repos. `check` without `--smart` makes
39	> no network calls at all.
40	
41	## Programmatic API
42	
43	```ts
44	import { validateSpec, draftGateSection, smartReview } from 'frai-gate';
45	
46	const result = validateSpec(await fs.readFile('FRAI-SPEC.md', 'utf8'));
47	// { verdict: 'PASS' | 'WARN' | 'BLOCK', tier, findings, gateSection }
48	```
49	
50	The companion agent skill lives in
51	[sebuzdugan/frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills)
52	(`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`).
53

1	# Responsible AI Gate - Design
2	
3	*Date: 2026-08-05 · Status: implemented*
4	
5	## What this adds
6	
7	Inspired by [addyosmani/agent-skills](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills) - a collection of
8	engineering skills that force AI coding agents through quality gates (spec → plan → build → verify) -
9	FRAI gains the **responsible-AI equivalent of that gate**, without replicating the generic lifecycle
10	skills. One gate, done deeply:
11	
12	> **No AI feature spec is complete without a Responsible AI Gate section, and nothing ships
13	> until the gate passes.**
14	
15	Three pieces:
16	
17	| Piece | Path | What it is |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| Skill | [sebuzdugan/frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) (moved out of this repo 2026-08-05) | An agent skill (agent-skills `SKILL.md` format, installable via `npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai`) that makes any coding agent write specs that include the RAI Gate |
20	| Spec template | `packages/frai-gate/assets/rai-spec-template.md` (canonical copy also in frai-skills) | Copy-paste spec template with the `## Responsible AI Gate` section built in |
21	| Pipeline | `packages/frai-gate/` | `frai-gate` - a Claude Agent SDK pipeline + deterministic validator that drafts, checks, and enforces the gate (CI-friendly) |
22	
23	## The gate: seven checks
24	
25	Aligned with frai-core's questionnaire dimensions (core / impact / data / performance / monitoring / bias)
26	plus the EU AI Act tiering already used by FRAI Chat:
27	
28	1. **Risk tier** - EU AI Act-aligned classification (prohibited / high / limited / minimal) with justification. High-risk requires a named human sign-off.
29	2. **Data provenance & privacy** - sources, PII handling, consent basis, retention.
30	3. **Human oversight** - automation level, override path, kill switch.
31	4. **Evaluation plan** - pre-ship metrics with numeric thresholds.
32	5. **Bias & fairness** - affected groups, mitigations, how tested.
33	6. **Monitoring & rollback** - production monitoring, degradation detection, rollback trigger.
34	7. **Transparency & incident response** - user disclosure of AI, incident owner and process.
35	
36	Verdicts: **PASS** (all checks complete) / **WARN** (complete but weak answers) / **BLOCK**
37	(missing sections, placeholders, or high-risk without sign-off). BLOCK exits non-zero for CI.
38	
39	## frai-gate pipeline (Claude Agent SDK)
40	
41	Two layers so it is useful with or without an API key:
42	
43	- **Deterministic layer (no key needed):** parses the spec markdown, verifies every gate
44	  subsection exists and is answered (no `TBD`/placeholder text), enforces the high-risk
45	  sign-off rule. Powers `frai-gate check` and CI.
46	- **Smart layer (Claude Agent SDK):** `query()` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` with
47	  read-only tools (`Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) scoped to the repo:
48	  - `frai-gate draft` - scans the codebase for AI indicators, then drafts a filled-in
49	    RAI Gate section grounded in what the code actually does.
50	  - `frai-gate check --smart` - after the deterministic pass, adversarially reviews each
51	    gate answer for quality (vague thresholds, untestable claims) and adds findings.
52	
53	Commands: `frai-gate init` (drop the template into the repo) · `frai-gate check <spec>` ·
54	`frai-gate draft [--out <file>]` · all support `--json`.
55	
56	## Decisions
57	
58	- **TypeScript package mirroring `frai-agent`** (tsc build, `dist/`, ESM) - matches monorepo conventions.
59	- **Claude Agent SDK, not LangChain** - the user asked for an Agent SDK pipeline; `frai-agent`
60	  (LangChain/OpenAI) stays untouched. The SDK's built-in Read/Glob/Grep tools replace custom scan
61	  plumbing, with `permissionMode` restricted and write tools disallowed.
62	- **Skill lives in `skills/`** at repo root so the standard `npx skills add` layout finds it, and
63	  a `/rai-spec` slash command is provided under `.claude/commands/` for Claude Code users.
64	- **Only one skill** - deliberately no spec/plan/build/test clones; agent-skills already covers those.
65

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. |
| `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. |
| `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. |

- `--scan` – run code scanning before questions.

- `--key <apiKey>` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally.
- `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs.
- `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`).
- `--show-config` – display key storage status.

Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON.

Guided API key storage. Supply `--key <apiKey>` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`.

Based on the bug analysis below, design an implementation plan to fix the `--ci` flag not being passed through the frai CLI to frai-gate.

**Bug Analysis:**
- File: packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts, lines 737-755
- The `gate` command uses `allowUnknownOption(true)` but doesn't define explicit option definitions
- When user runs `frai gate init --ci`, the `--ci` flag is consumed by Commander but not included in the variadic `args` parameter

- After fix, rebuild with `pnpm --filter frai build` and verify the workflow file is created

**Possible approaches:**
1. Define explicit options on the gate command and reconstruct flags when spawning frai-gate
2. Use a custom action handler that captures process.argv.slice() to pass raw arguments to frai-gate
3. Modify how the gate command is set up to preserve unknown options

Design the most minimal, maintainable fix that preserves the current command structure and properly passes all flags through. Consider:
- Which approach is simplest to implement and understand?
- Does it handle all flags that frai-gate might receive?
- How does it interact with Commander.js's behavior?

## Context
The `frai gate init --ci` command (when called through the frai CLI) was not creating the `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` file, though it did create `FRAI-SPEC.md`. The `gate` command in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts uses `allowUnknownOption(true)` without `.passThrough()`. This causes Commander.js to consume unknown options like `--ci` without including them in the variadic `args` parameter passed to the action handler. Only positional arguments like `['init']` reach frai-gate, losing the flag.

Add `.passThrough()` to the gate command definition. This tells Commander.js to pass all arguments (including unknown options) directly to the action handler.

**Change in packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts (around line 738):**
```typescript

  .command('gate [args...]')
  .description('Responsible AI Gate for specs: init | check <spec> [--smart] | draft. Delegates to frai-gate.')
  .passThrough()  // ← ADD THIS LINE
  .allowUnknownOption(true)
  .helpOption(false)
  .action(async (args: string[]) => {
    // ... rest unchanged
  });
```

This ensures that when a user runs `frai gate init --ci`, the `args` array will be `['init', '--ci']` instead of just `['init']`, which is what frai-gate expects.

**Why this approach:**
- Minimal one-line change
- Consistent with the `spec` command pattern already in the same file
- Maintains the existing architecture and doesn't change how frai-gate is invoked
- Future-proof: works for any flags frai-gate expects, not just `--ci`

## Implementation Plan: Fix `--ci` Flag Not Passed to frai-gate

### Problem Analysis

The bug occurs because:
1. **Current behavior**: The `gate` command uses `allowUnknownOption(true)` without explicitly defining option schemas
2. **Commander.js behavior**: When options are unknown, Commander parses them but doesn't include them in the variadic `args` parameter
3. **Result**: Only `['init']` is passed to frai-gate, not `['init', '--ci']`
4. **Impact**: frai-gate's `parseArgs()` never sees the `--ci` flag and skips creating `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml`

### Root Cause

In `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/pilot-steps-a/with/t1-flag-bug/r1/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 737-755):
- The action handler signature is `async (args: string[])` - it only captures variadic positional arguments
- Commander.js with `allowUnknownOption(true)` silently accepts but discards unknown flags
- The flags never reach the `spawnSync` call that executes frai-gate

### Recommended Approach: Explicit Options Reconstruction

This is the most minimal, maintainable solution that:
- Works correctly with Commander.js 11.x
- Explicitly documents all supported flags
- Automatically handles all frai-gate flags without custom parsing
- Preserves the current command structure

### Implementation Steps

1. **Add explicit option definitions** to the gate command
   - Define `--ci` (boolean)
   - Define `--out <file>` (string value)
   - Define `--smart` (boolean)
   - Define `--json` (boolean)
   - Define `--print` (boolean)
   - Keep `allowUnknownOption(true)` for forward compatibility

2. **Update the action handler signature**
   - Change from: `async (args: string[]) => {`
   - Change to: `async (args: string[], options: Record<string, any>) => {`
   - This allows access to both positional arguments and parsed options

3. **Reconstruct command arguments**
   - Start with the variadic positional args: `const gateArgs: string[] = [...(args ?? [])]`
   - Append flags from options object:
     ```typescript
     if (options.ci) gateArgs.push('--ci');
     if (options.out) gateArgs.push('--out', options.out);
     if (options.smart) gateArgs.push('--smart');
     if (options.json) gateArgs.push('--json');
     if (options.print) gateArgs.push('--print');
     ```

4. **Pass reconstructed args to frai-gate**
   - Replace `...(args ?? [])` with `...gateArgs` in the `spawnSync` call

### Why This Approach

**Advantages:**
- Minimal code change (only 15-20 lines modified)
- Works seamlessly with Commander.js 11.x
- Explicit and self-documenting - flags are visible in the help text
- Follows the pattern used by other commands in the codebase (`generate`, `scan`, etc.)
- Future-proof: any new frai-gate flags will require explicit additions (intentional coupling)
- No reliance on `process.argv` manipulation or custom parsing

**Trade-offs:**
- If frai-gate adds new flags, frai-cli must be updated
- However, this is acceptable given the dependency relationship

### Verification Plan

After implementation:
1. Rebuild: `pnpm --filter frai build`
2. Test the fix:
   ```bash
   frai gate init --ci
   ```
3. Verify output:
   - `FRAI-SPEC.md` created ✓
   - `.github/workflows/rai-gate.yml` created ✓ (this was missing before)

### Code Snapshot of Changes

The modified gate command definition will look like:

```typescript

  .command('gate [args...]')
  .description('Responsible AI Gate for specs: init | check <spec> [--smart] | draft. Delegates to frai-gate.')
  .option('--ci', 'Include CI workflow setup (init command)')
  .option('--out <file>', 'Output file path (init and draft commands)')
  .option('--smart', 'Add AI quality review (check command)')
  .option('--json', 'Machine-readable output (check command)')
  .option('--print', 'Print output instead of writing (draft command)')
  .allowUnknownOption(true)
  .helpOption(false)
  .action(async (args: string[], options: Record<string, any>) => {
    // ... resolve gateCli ...
    
    const gateArgs: string[] = [...(args ?? [])];
    if (options.ci) gateArgs.push('--ci');
    if (options.out) gateArgs.push('--out', options.out);
    if (options.smart) gateArgs.push('--smart');
    if (options.json) gateArgs.push('--json');
    if (options.print) gateArgs.push('--print');
    
    const { spawnSync } = await import('child_process');
    const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [gateCli, ...gateArgs], { stdio: 'inherit' });
    process.exit(result.status ?? 0);
  });
```
